events.title: FOMC decision, SEP/dot plot, Warsh press conference
events.why_it_matters: Markets now price ~77% odds of a 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% (Kalshi, Sept 14) after August CPI stayed at 3.4% y/y and payrolls beat; the dot plot and Warsh's guidance matter more than the decision itself.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the SEP dots show one or two 2026 hikes and whether Warsh signals a pause after September or an ongoing tightening cycle.

events.title: August CPI — inflation held at 3.4% y/y, locking in hike
events.why_it_matters: Consumer prices accelerated in August, removing the last obstacle to a September hike and cementing the hawkish repricing across rates and equities.
events.what_to_watch: Whether core services inflation cools in the September print (due mid-October) or confirms a sticky 3%+ regime.

events.title: August advance retail sales
events.why_it_matters: July retail sales fell 0.6% m/m; a second weak print would sharpen the stagflation narrative even as the Fed hikes into it.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the control group rebounds or confirms a softening US consumer ahead of holiday season.

events.title: Bank of Japan decision — hike to 1.25% widely expected
events.why_it_matters: Reuters reports the BOJ is set to hike 25bp to 1.25% with a faster tightening pace; a hike into a global risk-off, oil-shock backdrop is the classic yen-carry unwind trigger.
events.what_to_watch: Governor Ueda's guidance on the pace of further hikes and any JGB purchase-taper signals.

events.title: Bank of England decision — hold at 3.75% expected
events.why_it_matters: A hold is widely expected after the 6-3 July vote, but the oil surge has revived hike bets and three MPC members already voted to raise; UK CPI ~3.7% keeps a hike live.
events.what_to_watch: The vote split — a shift to 5-4 or 4-5 would move GBP and gilts sharply.

events.title: ECB 25bp hike to 2.50% delivered; fourth move in question
events.why_it_matters: The ECB hiked as expected and raised both inflation and growth forecasts, explicitly citing Iran-war energy inflation — a hawkish shift that pressures EU duration and cyclicals.
events.what_to_watch: Whether Lagarde signals an October pause or a fourth consecutive hike at the next meeting.

events.title: August PPI — in line, pipeline inflation intact
events.why_it_matters: Wholesale prices advanced in line with expectations, keeping the pipeline-inflation narrative alive into CPI and the FOMC.
events.what_to_watch: Whether energy pass-through shows up in September PPI after the oil spike.

events.title: August jobs report — 162k payrolls beat, unemployment 4.1%
events.why_it_matters: A blowout payrolls print removed the labor-market excuse for the Fed to stay on hold and drove hike odds sharply higher.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the September report (early October) shows any cooling from the oil shock.

events.title: China August activity data — industrial production, retail sales, FAI
events.why_it_matters: August PMI shrank for a second straight month and July IP/retail missed; another weak batch keeps pressure on Beijing for stimulus and weighs on global cyclicals and commodities.
events.what_to_watch: Whether property investment deterioration accelerates and whether services demand offsets weak goods consumption.

events.title: US-Iran tanker war; Brent ~$107, Hormuz traffic impaired
events.why_it_matters: Repeated US strikes on Iranian tankers and Iranian counterattacks have pushed Brent to ~$107 (+2.7% today) with the EIA estimating 5.7 mb/d shut in through end-2026 — a direct stagflationary shock.
events.what_to_watch: Any Iranian retaliation on Gulf infrastructure or a Hormuz closure, and Trump's comment that the war ends 'immediately' after the midterms.

events.title: Trump-Xi Washington summit
events.why_it_matters: Xi's state visit is the highest-stakes trade event of the quarter, covering tariffs, AI, Taiwan and the Iran war, and lands less than six weeks before the US midterms with the November truce expiry looming.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the leaders extend the tariff truce beyond November or leave it to lapse, and any Taiwan or AI-chip language.

events.title: US-Canada Section 338 tariff scope changes and import bans
events.why_it_matters: Tariff list changes take effect Sept 15 and outright import bans on Canadian dairy, alcohol, motorcycles and ATVs take effect Sept 29 with no USMCA exemption — a fresh supply-chain and pricing shock.
events.what_to_watch: Canadian retaliation and whether affected importers front-run the Sept 29 ban.

events.title: Government funding — House passed CR through midterms; Sept 30 deadline
events.why_it_matters: The House approved legislation to fund the government through the midterms, sharply reducing shutdown risk at the Sept 30 deadline, though the Senate still must act.
events.what_to_watch: Senate passage and any last-minute policy riders that could reopen the fight.

events.title: US midterm elections — divided-government expectations
events.why_it_matters: Strategists expect a divided government that limits major legislative change; positioning and policy-anticipation flows build through September and October.
events.what_to_watch: Polling shifts on House/Senate control and any sector-specific policy proposals gaining traction.

events.title: FedEx FQ1 2027 earnings
events.why_it_matters: The best single-company read on global goods demand and parcel pricing, arriving amid tariff-driven trade rerouting and a soft US consumer; consensus ~$4.21 EPS on ~$23.2bn revenue.
events.what_to_watch: Peak-season guidance and any commentary on tariff-driven volume shifts and the freight spin-off.

events.title: Micron FQ4 2026 earnings (AI memory catalyst)
events.why_it_matters: Billed as the key AI-memory catalyst of the year with HBM sold out through 2026, but the recent KOSPI memory-stock selloff on 'AI slowdown' fears raises the bar for guidance.
events.what_to_watch: HBM4 pricing, DRAM contract pricing and any sign of demand softening from the AI-slowdown debate.

events.title: Oracle FQ1 2027 earnings — beat, cloud infra +121%, backlog $638bn
events.why_it_matters: Oracle beat with 27% revenue growth and a $638bn backlog, a strong read on AI capex demand, though negative free cash flow and heavy debt raises raise funding questions.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the AI-infrastructure backlog converts to revenue and how the market treats the cash-burn profile.

events.title: Adobe FQ3 2026 earnings — record Q3, stock slipped
events.why_it_matters: Adobe reported record Q3 results and raised its outlook but the stock slipped — a bellwether for AI cannibalization of creative-software seats.
events.what_to_watch: Net-new ARR trends and whether AI features offset seat pressure.

events.title: Anthropic IPO — launch shifting toward mid-October
events.why_it_matters: Reuters reports the Anthropic IPO launch is shifting toward mid-October with a reported ~$2tn target valuation and Q3 profit projected above $1bn — the largest AI IPO test yet and a sentiment driver for the whole AI complex.
events.what_to_watch: The S-1 filing date and disclosed risk factors, which could crystallize AI-backlash and valuation concerns.

events.title: September quadruple witching / quarterly options expiry
events.why_it_matters: Quarterly expiry of index futures, index options, stock options and single-stock futures lands two days after the FOMC, amplifying volume and pinning risk around a binary macro event.
events.what_to_watch: Dealer gamma positioning and end-of-quarter rebalancing flows into the close.

events.title: KOSPI plunge — AI-slowdown debate hits memory stocks
events.why_it_matters: KOSPI fell over 3% to ~6,680 with foreign investors selling 3.3tn won as Samsung and SK Hynix slid on AI-slowdown fears, a live read-through to US semis and the AI trade.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the memory selloff broadens to US semis and whether it is positioning-driven or a genuine demand signal.

events.title: South Korea semiconductor export boom — chips top 400tn won
events.why_it_matters: Korean chip exports rose 169.6% y/y and topped 400tn won for the first time, but China's CXMT is gaining DRAM share and a stronger won threatens Samsung/SK Hynix margins — a two-sided signal for the memory cycle.
events.what_to_watch: September export data (Oct 1) and whether CXMT share gains accelerate.

events.title: Taiwan/TSMC chip-diplomacy tension ahead of Trump-Xi summit
events.why_it_matters: Taiwan is leveraging TSMC as diplomatic capital while China conducts precision-strike drills; Taiwan is likely on the summit agenda, making it a tail-risk for the entire semiconductor supply chain.
events.what_to_watch: Any Chinese military escalation around the summit and whether Taiwan appears in joint statements.

events.title: OPEC+ September output hike completed; next meeting watch
events.why_it_matters: OPEC+ completed its rollback of voluntary cuts with a September hike, but the Iran war has overwhelmed supply-side fundamentals and kept Brent above $107.
events.what_to_watch: Whether OPEC+ pauses or accelerates hikes at its next meeting and whether spare capacity can offset Hormuz disruption.

events.title: US-China tariff truce expiry (November 2026)
events.why_it_matters: The late-2025 tactical truce expires in November 2026 and Treasury Secretary Bessent has signaled the US is 'not in a hurry' to extend it, making the Sept 24 summit the key venue for a decision.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the summit produces a truce extension or a lapse that re-escalates tariffs into year-end.

events.title: September PDUFA cluster — 11 FDA decisions
events.why_it_matters: September is the busiest PDUFA month of H2 with 11 FDA target action dates across rare disease, oncology, neurology and hematology — binary events for small- and mid-cap biotech.
events.what_to_watch: Approval or CRL decisions on the priority-review oncology and neurology filings.

events.title: Data-center power demand vs. grid constraints (Texas halt)
events.why_it_matters: Texas halted powering some data centers over 'ghost demand' concerns while clean-energy groups push for scrutiny of data-center energy costs — a growing constraint on AI buildout and a driver for Utilities and power infrastructure.
events.what_to_watch: State-level interconnection policy and whether power availability slows AI data-center timelines.

events.title: Atlantic hurricane season — well below-normal, but Edouard hit Gulf
events.why_it_matters: CSU forecasts a well below-normal season under intensifying El Niño, but Tropical Storm Edouard struck the Gulf Coast on Aug 31, a reminder of refinery and offshore production risk during peak season.
events.what_to_watch: Any new Gulf system threatening refineries or LNG infrastructure through late September.

events.title: US Supreme Court
